result.question: We have a rule for Transformer 1 at MAIN: if it reaches IEEE C57.104 Condition 3, we plan an outage and go to monthly oil sampling. Check whether we're there. Work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. If it's Condition 3 or 4, do the following. Look at the MAIN schedule for the 21 days after the latest sample date and propose the 2-day outage window with the fewest scheduled work orders. Create a priority 1 outage and inspection work order for that window, with a note to notify the manufacturer. Create a separate work order for the next monthly DGA sample, dated 30 days after the latest sample. If it's Condition 2, don't plan an outage. Just create a quarterly resample work order. If it's Condition 1, create nothing and tell me how many ppm of headroom we have to 1921. In every case, first check for open work orders on Transformer 1 that already cover an outage or DGA sampling, and don't duplicate them. If one exists, reference it and explain how your recommendation differs. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
## Result

**TDCG (latest sample, 2024-01-19):**
| Gas | ppm |
|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2850 |
| Methane | 7400 |
| Ethane | 5470 |
| Ethylene | 16650 |
| Acetylene | 7 |
| CO | 32 |
| **TDCG** | **32,299 ppm** |

None of the six gases was null in the latest sample, so no values were carried forward.

**Condition:** With TDCG = 32,299 ppm, this is **above 4,630 ppm → Condition 4**, which is within your "Condition 3 or 4" trigger. Your rule is met: plan an outage and move to monthly oil sampling.

**Existing open work orders on Transformer 1:**
- **WO 1000051** (WAPPR, P1, PdM): "OLTC inspection — Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking)". This covers an outage-type inspection, so I did not duplicate it. My recommendation differs as follows: it targets the OLTC specifically for suspected tap-changer wear/coking. Your DGA result (TDCG 32,299 ppm, dominated by ethylene 16,650 and methane 7,400) is consistent with a severe thermal fault, which an OLTC inspection is a reasonable response to — but a full Condition 4-level outage should also cover a broader inspection scope (windings, core, oil, cooling) and an explicit manufacturer notification, which 1000051's notes do not call out. I recommend updating 1000051 to reflect the broader Condition 4 scope and manufacturer notification rather than creating a duplicate outage WO.
- No existing open work order covers DGA/oil sampling, so a new monthly DGA sample WO is warranted.

**Scheduling check:** The MAIN schedule for the 21 days after 2024-01-19 (through 2024-02-09) shows **0 scheduled work orders**. With a clean calendar, every 2-day window ties at zero; the earliest window is **2024-01-19 to 2024-01-21**.

**Actions I attempted but could not complete — the work order creation tool returned HTTP 403 (Forbidden) on every attempt, including a minimal test:**
1. Priority 1 outage/inspection WO for 2024-01-19 → 2024-01-21 with note to notify the manufacturer — **not created (403 error)**.
2. Monthly DGA sample WO dated 2024-02-18 (30 days after 2024-01-19) — **not created (403 error)**.

I did not update WO 1000051 either, since write access appears blocked.

**Recommended manual follow-up (blocked here):**
- Update WO 1000051 to include Condition 4 scope (full outage inspection, not just OLTC) and a manufacturer notification note; or create a separate P1 outage WO for 2024-01-19 → 2024-01-21 if you prefer to keep 1000051 OLTC-specific.
- Create a monthly DGA sampling work order dated 2024-02-18, and repeat monthly while the unit remains in Condition 3/4.
